title: Intel tool responses are unbounded: THREATREP is 1.1 MB at 36 tracks, breaking the harness path
description:
MEASURED on a booted stack (default theater, 36 tracks in the persisted store):
  uav_list_tracks            198,812 bytes
  uav_target_report (INTREP) 411,020 bytes
  mission_threat_assessment  1,144,394 bytes

CONSEQUENCE: the python MCP CLIENT fails the call with 'MCPError: SSE stream ended without a response' (instantly, every variant: plain, survey=False, dry_run=True). The SERVER is fine - a raw curl POST returns HTTP 200 with a valid THREATREP - so this is purely a size problem on the response. scripts/demo_laptop.sh therefore FAILS at exit 2 on its final step: the mission flies to 100%% and then the threat assessment kills the run. That is the shipped one-command demo.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE CLIENT BUG: the consumer is an LLM harness. A 1.1 MB tool result is unusable even if the transport carried it - it would exhaust the context window in a single call. uav_target_report is the primary reporting artifact and is already 411 KB.

ROOT CAUSE: the report is unbounded in the track count and every assessment carries its full traceable sub-score breakdown (capability formula, engagement geometry, intent indicators, per-element evidence). M13 legitimately requires that traceability - the defect is that it is the DEFAULT response rather than an opt-in detail level. It also grows without limit because the track store persists across runs (M11/M12 working as designed), so a long-lived store makes every intel call worse.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (decide deliberately):
  - default: a summary - counts by threat level, the top N assessments, ids only for the rest
  - full traceability behind detail='full', a per-track call, or the uav://reports/{id} resource
  - cap/paginate anything that scales with the track store, and SAY when output was truncated
    (never silently - see the M1 coverage lesson)
  - consider a max-response-size guard so a tool can never again return something no client can read

REPRO:
  ./scripts/demo_laptop.sh            # fails exit 2 at the threat assessment
  curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<mcp>/mcp -H 'Authorization: Bearer dev-token' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"mission_threat_assessment","arguments":{"vehicle":"Drone1"}}}' | wc -c
notes:
FIXED SO FAR (threat.py + targets.py, both free of Wave-6 ownership):
  assess_area(detail='summary'|'full', top_n=SUMMARY_TOP_N)  - summary drops the expandable
    'assessment' sub-objects and the 'evidence' list (a flattened duplicate of them) and hoists the
    per-contact ISR authority note to the report. Every flat traceable score component survives.
  intrep_report(detail=..., top_n=...) - summary drops each contact's nested 'confidence' derivation,
    keeping confidence_level/confidence_score.
  Both: contacts past top_n are listed as compact rows ('omitted' / 'contacts_omitted') and named in
  a 'truncation' string; INTREP counts, confidence_summary and gaps are still computed over ALL
  contacts, never only the expanded ones. An unknown detail level RAISES rather than defaulting.
  MEASURED at 31 tracks: THREATREP 319,792 -> 18,876 bytes (17x); INTREP 220,772 -> 47,364 (4.7x).
  8 new tests in test_threat.py::TestThreatrepSize and test_targets.py::TestIntrepSize; the two that

title: Close the ceiling / min-AGL bypasses on takeoff and ground-altitude waypoints
description: PLAN.md 4.5 (ceiling / min AGL). GAP_REGISTER.md MAJOR [safety-fuel], blocks_goal True. EVIDENCE: three holes in mcp/godseye_uav/safety.py. (1) safety.py:152 guards min AGL with "if 0 < alt_agl < self.min_agl_m", so an alt_agl of exactly 0 or negative never violates - flying into the ground passes the check. (2) safety.py:159 defaults a waypoint with no altitude key to 0, so such a waypoint always passes. (3) takeoff altitude bypasses the ceiling check entirely. REQUIRED: violate on any altitude below the floor including 0 and negatives; reject a missing altitude rather than defaulting it; run takeoff altitude through the ceiling check. notes:
RECONCILIATION AUDIT (wave-5): NOT CLOSED, and the bypass is WORSE than this bead originally described. Raised to P1 - this is a live safety-gate hole, not a latent one.

THE KEY-NAME BYPASS (new, not in the original bead). SafetyEnvelope.check_route (safety.py:676) reads:
    float(wp.get('alt_agl', wp.get('alt_m', 0)))
It never reads alt_agl_m - which is the spelling uav_fly_route's OWN tool description mandates (server.py:4369-4372: 'Each waypoint is {lat, lon, alt_agl_m}', 'TOOL_CONTRACT 4.1: never a bare alt_m'). So a harness route written against the DOCUMENTED contract has every waypoint altitude read as 0, and both the ceiling and min-AGL checks pass trivially.

REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY (SafetyEnvelope ceiling 120 m, min_agl 30 m):
    alt_agl_m = 500 -> []                              <-- 500 m passes a 120 m ceiling
    alt_m     = 500 -> ['wp0:ceiling(500m>120m)']
    alt_agl   = 500 -> ['wp0:ceiling(500m>120m)']
    alt_agl_m = 5   -> []                              <-- 5 m passes a 30 m floor
uav_fly_route (server.py:4381) hands raw waypoints straight to _gate -> check_route (server.py:2488) with NO normalization, so this reaches the gate live. Mission-planned routes are unaffected because missions.py:270-271 emits BOTH alt_m and alt_agl_m - which is almost certainly why no test caught it.

NO DOWNSTREAM BACKSTOP: in-flight ceiling is alarm-only under BREACH_DOCTRINE (safety.py:454) and does not force RTB.

AGAINST THIS BEAD'S THREE REQUIRED ITEMS:
 (1) NOT fixed - safety.py:669 is still verbatim 'if 0 < alt_agl < self.min_agl_m', so check_point(..., 0.0) and check_point(..., -50.0) both return [].

The EGM96 repair (godseye-6ko.2) is real and correct, but it works only in this checkout's .venv: (1) pyproject.toml:20-21 puts pyproj in an OPTIONAL 'geo' extra, so a plain 'pip install .' does not get it; (2) the vendored egm96-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl in the repo root is referenced nowhere in pyproject.toml, so the pure-Python cross-check source is not installed either; (3) the 2.7 MB grid mcp/godseye_uav/data/us_nga_egm96_15.tif has no package_data / include entry, so it is not packaged. Since geo.py:317-327 now correctly RAISES GeoidUnavailableError rather than silently falling back to the latitude-only approximation, a clean install fails closed - launch.py refuses to boot on a degraded datum. That is the right failure mode but the wrong default: the fix for the silent fallback turned a wrong-answer bug into an install-time hard stop. REQUIRED: make pyproj a hard dependency (or vendor the egm96 wheel as one), add the .tif to package data so it ships with the distribution, and add a test that imports the package from an installed wheel in a clean env and asserts geoid_source() reports the grid.

title: Python test suite takes ~25 minutes, slowing every change
description: EVIDENCE: 954 tests collected (pytest --collect-only -q, 1.07 s to collect). Individual module timings measured during this audit: tests/test_fake_airsim.py 42 passed in 139 s, tests/test_realism.py 41 passed in 209 s, tests/test_tasking.py 29 passed in 16.5 s. The suite went 106 -> ~954 tests across five waves and the wall time grew with it. The dominant cost is real-time integration: many tests boot a FakeAirSim over a real msgpack-rpc socket and then POLL A 50 Hz PHYSICS LOOP IN WALL-CLOCK TIME (fake_airsim.py:403-406 _physics_loop, _integrate at :421) - waiting for arrivals, for object motion, for fuel to burn down, for watchdog windows (DEFAULT_NO_PROGRESS_S = 120.0). IMPACT: the feedback loop is long enough that changes get made without running the suite, which is how the gaps this audit found (unrehydrated intel stores, no PIP) survived five green waves. REQUIRED (pick what fits): a sim time-scale / clock-injection knob so the physics loop can run faster than real time in tests; pytest-xdist parallelism across modules (they already boot independent sims on ephemeral ports); and mark the genuinely slow wire tests so a fast default run and a full gate run are separable. Measure before and after - the goal is a sub-2-minute default run, with the full suite still green.

title: Active-theater block drops ground_elevation_msl_m and the enforced AO, so the GEV panel geofences against its own table row
description: EVIDENCE: normalizeActiveTheater (gods-eye-view/src/sources/live/uav.js:480-518) returns a fixed whitelist — {known, id, label, reason, mismatch, source, atMs} — and drops every other field of the active block. The bridge DOES publish the two that matter (mcp/godseye_uav/bridge.py:85), and the doc comment at src/sources/live/uav.js:457 explicitly lists ground_elevation_msl_m and ao as published. Neither field then exists anywhere in gods-eye-view/src (grep for ground_elevation/groundElevation hits only unrelated src/locations.js; active?.ao has no hits). CONSEQUENCE: the panel falls back to its own bundled table row for both — uavMissionPanel.js:526 (const c = t?.ao || []) and :532 (t?.demo?.polygon?.length ? t.demo.polygon : t?.ao || []), where t comes from theaters.get(...). So the operator plans and geofences against the CLIENT's idea of the AO and ground elevation, not the envelope the server actually enforces. That is the same drift class as godseye-nyo.3, just moved from two hand-typed tables to a table row versus a served block, and it undercuts the purpose of publishing the active block at all. REQUIRED: carry ground_elevation_msl_m and the enforced AO polygon through normalizeActiveTheater, prefer them over the table row wherever the panel plans or geofences, and make a disagreement between served block and table row visible rather than silently resolved (BRIDGE_CONTRACT.md:160).

title: createTheaterRegistry().get(id) silently resolves an unknown theater id to the table default
description: EVIDENCE: gods-eye-view/src/ui/uavTheaters.js:334 — 'get: (id) => table.theaters[id] || table.theaters[table.defaultId] || null'. An id the table does not carry silently becomes the DEFAULT theater row. Consumed by theater() at src/ui/uavMissionPanel.js:402-404, which feeds missionParams() (:522-537), so an unknown id would quietly plan and geofence against the wrong AO. This is the exact class of defect the rest of the theater work was built to prevent: normalizeTheaterTable (src/sources/live/uav.js:544-551) deliberately keeps an unknown active id marked inTable:false 'because silently resolving it to the default would hide the very mismatch it proves', and BRIDGE_CONTRACT.md:158 says a running theater the client's table does not carry must be REPORTED, never resolved to the default. get() contradicts both. CURRENTLY UNREACHABLE (callers pre-check inTable), so this is a latent live fallback, not an active bug — which is why it is P2 rather than P1. REQUIRED: return null (or an explicit not-in-table marker) for an unknown id and make every caller handle it visibly. NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: the current behavior is locked in by a passing test named 'an unknown theater id resolves to the table default, never to nothing' in src/ui/uavTheaters.test.mjs — that test has to change with the fix.

title: GEV panel stops re-asking the bridge once a theater is learned - a bridge restarted onto a different theater is never adopted until page reload
description: EVIDENCE: gods-eye-view/src/ui/uavMissionPanel.js:810-819, adoptRunningTheater(). The doc comment states the limit outright: 'once a running theater has been learned the panel stops asking, so a bridge restarted onto a different theater is not picked up until the page reloads.' The retry loop exists precisely because the panel usually loads before the bridge (adoptTries), but it latches on first success. createTheaterRegistry().refresh() (src/ui/uavTheaters.js:344-379) is itself safely re-callable and already preserves prior knowledge on a blip, so the fix is in the panel's stop condition, not the registry. IMPACT: during a demo the operator restarts the MCP/bridge onto a new theater and the panel silently keeps geofencing and plotting against the old one - the exact class of defect INTEGRATION_FINDINGS.md UI-1 was raised for. REQUIRED: keep polling the running-theater block on a slow cadence (or re-ask on bridge reconnect / sim_reset), adopt a changed id through the same visible path as first adoption, and keep the two deliberate limits (selection moves, camera does not; a bridge that publishes no active theater is not an error).

title: Threat score is an additive weighted sum, not capability x intent, and its components are not returned
description: PLAN.md:173 section 4.6(d) / M13(d): "score = capability x intent, each component traceable". GAP_REGISTER.md MAJOR [intel-tracks-threat], blocks_goal True. EVIDENCE: threat.py:78 - score = min(1.0, 0.5 * base + 0.3 * envelope_factor + 0.2 * intent). The output dict (threat.py:81-92) returns intent but never base/capability or the envelope factor, so the score is neither the specified form nor traceable. VERIFIED PATHOLOGY of the additive form: a stationary SAM co-located with the observer and intent exactly 0.0 still scores 0.8 and is reported as threat_level critical, because the additive terms floor the score regardless of intent. A multiplicative form would return 0. REQUIRED: capability x intent with every component returned alongside the score. Small change, large correctness impact on every assessment the operator sees. FILES: mcp/godseye_uav/threat.py.
